data.title: XTI Aerospace Faces Default Waivers and Debt Restructuring
data.description:
The latest update is out from XTI Aerospace ( (XTIA) ).

On November 10, 2025, XTI Drones Holdings issued two seller promissory notes totaling nearly $12 million to finance the acquisitions of Drone Nerds and Anzu Robotics, with interest originally set at 7.25% and final maturity on November 10, 2026. Required principal installments of $1.38 million under the Drone Nerds note and $120,000 under the Anzu Robotics note, due by September 30, 2026, were not paid.

Because those missed payments were not cured within ten days, events of default were triggered under both notes on October 11, 2026, when the aggregate outstanding principal, including capitalized interest, stood at about $4.51 million. The default raised interest to 9.25% and gave the note holders the right to accelerate all amounts due, although as of the latest filing they had not exercised these remedies.

The default on the Drone Nerds note also caused cross-defaults under the $20 million secured revolving Credit Agreement with JPMorgan Chase, putting the facility into a state where the lender is no longer obligated to extend further credit and may restrict dividends, distributions and certain debt payments. As of October 16, 2026, approximately $8.4 million was outstanding under the Credit Agreement, and while the lender has not yet moved to accelerate or enforce remedies, additional events of default may be asserted.

XTI Aerospace and its subsidiaries have negotiated terms for a temporary waiver of the note defaults with the sellers and plan to pursue restructuring of the seller notes, while also seeking waivers of the Credit Agreement defaults from JPMorgan Chase. The company acknowledges that if waivers or restructurings are not achieved, the note holders and lender could accelerate obligations and enforce security interests, which XTI currently lacks the liquidity to repay in full, posing a material risk to its funding capacity, financial condition and ongoing operations.
